chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Jahm ibn Humaid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you not visit the ruler of these people?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Why?' I said: 'To save my religion.' He said: 'You have made a firm decision regarding that.' I said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'Now your religion is safe for you.'

key_terms.سَلِمَ لَكَ دِينُكَ: Your religion is safe for you
key_terms.هَؤُلَاءِ: These people (referring to the ruling dynasty)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Shia scholars avoid the Umayyad and Abbasid rulers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of *al-ghishyah* (avoidance) of political rulers as a means of preserving religious integrity, a concept central to Shia political quietism. The Imam’s affirmation that the companion’s deliberate flight has 'saved his religion' underscores the theological priority of spiritual purity over political engagement or compromise with unjust authority. This narrative provides a foundational scriptural basis for the Shia tradition of maintaining distance from state power to avoid religious dilution.
